title: Pro-rata per-vector + time-decay batch credit pilot for embeddings & rerank
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Overview: We will run a controlled pilot that introduces a pro-rata per-vector pricing variant combined with time-decay batch credits to better align unit economics with real-world embedding/rerank traffic patterns. The pilot aims to reduce marginal token-equivalent cost for customers with bursty, time-localized embedding workloads while preserving revenue per unit for steady-volume customers. This is explicitly targeted at customers using large rerank batches and churny embedding ingestion (search indexing, daily bulk reranks).

Goals and hypotheses: 
- Hypothesis 1: A pro-rata model (billing fractional vector units for partial batch slots) will increase conversions for mid-volume buyers (10k-1M vectors/month) by ~12% vs. flat-per-vector pricing.
- Hypothesis 2: Adding time-decay batch credits (credits that step down over a 72-hour window) will allow customers to smooth peak loads into lower unit cost without increasing long-term revenue leakage.
- Success metrics: conversion uplift (trial->paid) for target cohort, ARPU for embedding customers, average effective price per vector, change in burst-induced peak GPU utilization, model-unit economics (revenue per GPU-hour).

Experiment design: 
- Variant A: Control (current per-vector pricing).
- Variant B: Pro-rata per-vector with 1/1000 granularity + soft cap (max 1.0 vector credit per input vector).
- Variant C: Pro-rata per-vector + 72-hour time-decay batch credits (credits applied to batches within N hours, decaying 100%->50%->25% over windows).
- Traffic: Randomized assignment for new trials and a stratified sample of existing customers (opt-in for enterprise via sales).
- Duration: 10 weeks (6 week run + 4 week monitoring).

Billing and contract considerations: 
- Contract language updates required for Reserved/Dedicated customers to clarify pro-rata rounding and refund mechanics.
- QSA/Enterprise questionnaire: Need to provide a customer-facing description of how credits are tracked, stored, and audited. Legal requested canonical wording and a short one-pager for e-contracts.

Data & telemetry: 
- Instrumentation: per-request vector-count tagging, batch_id, customer_tier, credit_applied_flag, timestamp.
- Dashboards: Conversion funnel, ARPU, unit-cost by cohort, GPU-hour correlation by hour.

Risk & mitigations: 
- Risk: Revenue leakage from aggressive credit stacking. Mitigation: soft caps and throttles, revenue delta daily monitoring with automated rollback.
- Risk: Complexity in invoicing + customer confusion. Mitigation: clear billing previews in Console, explanatory email flows, and sales enablement doc.
- Risk: Enterprise compliance concerns about immutable billing records. Mitigation: append immutable audit logs and KMS-backed signing for credit issuance records (Security/Legal review).

Deliverables: 
- PRD (this doc + roadmap section) and experiment playbook.
- Console billing preview UI mockups and API changes for pro-rata reporting.
- Billing pipeline changes for fractional unit aggregation and batch-credit decay logic.
- QSA pack updates and legal contract language.

rollout_plan: Start with opt-in enterprise pilots (Sales-sourced) + a randomized 10% sample of new self-serve trials. Week 0-1: light load validation and billing sanity checks. Week 2-3: expand to full cohort. Ongoing: monitor revenue delta, dispute rate, and utilization. If revenue delta exceeds -5% daily for two consecutive days or dispute rate >2x baseline for a week, auto-trigger rollback. After 6-week collection window, run uplift analysis and finance QA to decide go/no-go for wider rollout.

Attach sample log schema and example invoice lines. Legal requested a 'plain English' one-pager for customer-facing docs.
acceptance_criteria: Billing pipeline correctly aggregates fractional vector usage and emits invoices with rounded totals matching finance simulation within 0.5%
Console shows billing preview for eligible customers with clear credit decay visualization
Security has signed off on audit log format and KMS signing (security_review_required=false or signed)
No automated rollback triggers for majority (>90%) of pilot days
Statistically significant conversion uplift or neutral revenue impact demonstrated after 6-week window
